title: User Vault: what it uses
lede: One arrow for each component this feature lists. The steps reuse the feature's own "how it works" text; nothing here is a new claim. Internal and confidential: this text comes from an internal Ping deck and has not been tested on our tenant.

steps.title: Per-user vault
steps.what: User Vault is a private credential store per user, injected into that user's backend calls at request time, so the backend sees who actually acted.
steps.why: Shared service accounts break attribution, because every action looks the same in the target system's logs.

steps.title: Self-service only, no admin override
steps.what: There is no administrator override, and no admin, auditor or support role can read another user's credentials through the API.
steps.why: Shared service accounts break attribution, because every action looks the same in the target system's logs.

steps.title: AES-GCM encryption at rest
steps.what: Values are encrypted at rest with AES-GCM and a unique nonce per value.
steps.why: Shared service accounts break attribution, because every action looks the same in the target system's logs.

steps.title: AWS Secrets Manager with KMS or HashiCorp Vau…
steps.what: The key is resolved at startup from AWS Secrets Manager with KMS envelope decryption, or from HashiCorp Vault on premises, with a compiled-in development key only as fallback.
steps.why: Shared service accounts break attribution, because every action looks the same in the target system's logs.
